                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# 7. Adding Authentication\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Most modern apps need a way to create and authenticate users. Wasp makes this as easy as possible with its first-class auth support.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To add users to your app, you must:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [ ] Create a `User` Entity.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [ ] Tell Wasp to use the *Username and Password* authentication.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [ ] Add login and signup pages.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [ ] Update the main page to require authentication.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [ ] Add a relation between `User` and `Task` entities.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [ ] Modify your Queries and Actions so users can only see and modify their tasks.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [ ] Add a logout button.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Creating a User Entity\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since Wasp manages authentication, it will create [the auth related entities](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities) for you in the background. Nothing to do here!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You must only add the `User` Entity to keep track of who owns which tasks:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```prisma title="schema.prisma"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'model User {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id Int @id @default(autoincrement())\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Adding Auth to the Project\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Next, tell Wasp to use full-stack [authentication](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { action, app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getTasks } from "./src/queries" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { createTask, updateTask } from "./src/actions" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  auth: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // Tells Wasp which entity to use for storing users.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    userEntity: "User",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    methods: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      // Enable username and password auth.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      usernameAndPassword: {},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m"    // We'll see how this is used in a bit.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'    onAuthFailedRedirectTo: "/login",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("RootRoute", "/", page(MainPage)),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    query(getTasks, { entities: ["Task"] }),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    action(createTask, { entities: ["Task"] }),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    action(updateTask, { entities: ["Task"] }),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Don't forget to update the database schema by running:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```sh\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db migrate-dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By doing this, Wasp will create:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Auth UI](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/ui) with login and signup forms.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- A `logout()` action.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- A React hook `useAuth()`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `context.user` for use in Queries and Actions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp also supports authentication using [Google](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/google), [GitHub](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/github), and [email](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email), with more on the way!\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Adding Login and Signup Pages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp creates the login and signup forms for us, but we still need to define the pages to display those forms on. We'll start by declaring the pages in the Wasp file:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { action, app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { SignupPage } from "./src/SignupPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { LoginPage } from "./src/LoginPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getTasks } from "./src/queries" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { createTask, updateTask } from "./src/actions" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("RootRoute", "/", page(MainPage)),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("SignupRoute", "/signup", page(SignupPage)),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("LoginRoute", "/login", page(LoginPage)),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // ... existing queries and actions\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Great, Wasp now knows these pages exist!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's the React code for the pages you've just imported:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/LoginPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { Link } from "react-router";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { LoginForm } from "wasp/client/auth";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const LoginPage = () => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <div style={{ maxWidth: "400px", margin: "0 auto" }}>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <LoginForm />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <br />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <span>\n'[39m +
                      [32m`        I don't have an account yet (<Link to="/signup">go to signup</Link>).\n`[39m +
                      [32m'      </span>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  );\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The signup page is very similar to the login page:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/SignupPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { Link } from "react-router";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { SignupForm } from "wasp/client/auth";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const SignupPage = () => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <div style={{ maxWidth: "400px", margin: "0 auto" }}>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <SignupForm />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <br />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <span>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        I already have an account (<Link to="/login">go to login</Link>).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      </span>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  );\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::tip[Type-safe links]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Since you are using Typescript, you can benefit from using Wasp's type-safe `Link` component and the `routes` object. Check out the [type-safe links docs](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/advanced/links) for more details.\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Update the Main Page to Require Auth\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We don't want users who are not logged in to access the main page, because they won't be able to create any tasks. So let's make the page private by requiring the user to be logged in:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { action, app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { SignupPage } from "./src/SignupPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { LoginPage } from "./src/LoginPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getTasks } from "./src/queries" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { createTask, updateTask } from "./src/actions" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("RootRoute", "/", page(MainPage, {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      authRequired: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    })),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // ... existing routes, queries, and actions\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Now that auth is required for this page, unauthenticated users will be redirected to `/login`, as we specified with `auth.onAuthFailedRedirectTo`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Additionally, when `authRequired` is `true`, the page's React component will be provided a `user` object as prop.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/MainPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { AuthUser } from "wasp/auth";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ... existing imports\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const MainPage = ({ user }: { user: AuthUser }) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const { data: tasks, isLoading, error } = useQuery(getTasks);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Ok, time to test this out. Navigate to the main page (`/`) of the app. You'll get redirected to `/login`, where you'll be asked to authenticate.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Since we just added users, you don't have an account yet. Go to the signup page and create one. You'll be sent back to the main page where you will now be able to see the TODO list!\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's check out what the database looks like. Start the Prisma Studio:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```shell\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db studio\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'![Database demonstration - password hashing](https://wasp.sh/img/wasp_user_in_db.gif)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You'll notice that we now have a `User` entity in the database alongside the `Task` entity.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"However, you will notice that if you try logging in as different users and creating some tasks, all users share the same tasks. That's because you haven't yet updated the queries and actions to have per-user tasks. Let's do that next.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You might notice some extra Prisma models like `Auth`, `AuthIdentity` and `Session` that Wasp created for you. You don't need to care about these right now, but if you are curious, you can read more about them [here](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Defining a User-Task Relation\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"First, let's define a one-to-many relation between users and tasks (check the [Prisma docs on relations](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-schema/data-model/relations)):\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```prisma title="schema.prisma"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'model User {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id    Int    @id @default(autoincrement())\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  tasks Task[]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'model Task {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id          Int     @id @default(autoincrement())\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  description String\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  isDone      Boolean @default(false)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  user        User?   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  userId      Int?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As always, you must migrate the database after changing the Entities:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```sh\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db migrate-dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::note\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We made `user` and `userId` in `Task` optional (via `?`) because that allows us to keep the existing tasks, which don't have a user assigned, in the database.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This isn't recommended because it allows an unwanted state in the database (what is the purpose of the task not belonging to anybody?) and normally we would not make these fields optional.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Instead, we would do a data migration to take care of those tasks, even if it means just deleting them all. However, for this tutorial, for the sake of simplicity, we will stick with this.\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Updating Operations to Check Authentication\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Next, let's update the queries and actions to forbid access to non-authenticated users and to operate only on the currently logged-in user's tasks:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/queries.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { Task } from "wasp/entities";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { HttpError } from "wasp/server";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { GetTasks } from "wasp/server/operations";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const getTasks: GetTasks<void, Task[]> = async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  if (!context.user) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    throw new HttpError(401);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return context.entities.Task.findMany({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    where: { user: { id: context.user.id } },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    orderBy: { id: "asc" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  });\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/actions.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { Task } from "wasp/entities";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { HttpError } from "wasp/server";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { CreateTask, UpdateTask } from "wasp/server/operations";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type CreateTaskPayload = Pick<Task, "description">;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const createTask: CreateTask<CreateTaskPayload, Task> = async (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  args,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  context,\n'[39m +
                      [32m') => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  if (!context.user) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    throw new HttpError(401);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return context.entities.Task.create({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    data: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      description: args.description,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      user: { connect: { id: context.user.id } },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  });\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type UpdateTaskPayload = Pick<Task, "id" | "isDone">;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const updateTask: UpdateTask<\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  UpdateTaskPayload,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  { count: number }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> = async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  if (!context.user) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    throw new HttpError(401);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return context.entities.Task.updateMany({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    where: { id: args.id, user: { id: context.user.id } },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    data: { isDone: args.isDone },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  });\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::note\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Due to how Prisma works, we had to convert `update` to `updateMany` in `updateTask` action to be able to specify the user id in `where`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'With these changes, each user should have a list of tasks that only the'[39m... 2317 more characters
                  }
                ]
              },
              providerOptions: {
                vertex: {
                  thoughtSignature: [32m''[39m
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          role: [32m'assistant'[39m,
          content: [
            {
              type: [32m'tool-call'[39m,
              toolCallId: [32m'CdRxEN6DKLogxoA6'[39m,
              toolName: [32m'webFetch'[39m,
              input: {
                url: [32m'https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities.md'[39m
              },
              providerOptions: {
                vertex: {
                  thoughtSignature: [32m''[39m
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          role: [32m'tool'[39m,
          content: [
            {
              type: [32m'tool-result'[39m,
              toolCallId: [32m'CdRxEN6DKLogxoA6'[39m,
              toolName: [32m'webFetch'[39m,
              output: {
                type: [32m'content'[39m,
                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'Title: \n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'URL Source: https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities.md\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Markdown Content:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://wasp.sh/llms.txt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'---\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Accessing User Data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"First, we'll check out the most practical info: **how to access the user's data in your app**.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Then, we'll dive into the details of the **auth entities** that Wasp creates behind the scenes to store the user's data. For auth each method, Wasp needs to store different information about the user. For example, username for [Username & password](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass) auth, email verification status for [Email](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email) auth, and so on.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We'll also show you how you can use these entities to create a custom signup action.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Accessing the Auth Fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you receive the `user` object [on the client or the server](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#accessing-the-logged-in-user), it will contain all the user fields you defined in the `User` entity in the `schema.prisma` file. In addition to that, it will also contain all the auth-related fields that Wasp stores. This includes things like the `username` or the email verification status. In Wasp, this data is called the `AuthUser` object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### `AuthUser` Object Fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All the `User` fields you defined will be present at the top level of the `AuthUser` object. The auth-related fields will be on the `identities` object. For each auth method you enable, there will be a separate data object in the `identities` object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `AuthUser` object will change depending on which auth method you have enabled in the Wasp file. For example, if you enabled the email auth and Google auth, it would look something like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**User Signed Up with Google**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the user has only the Google identity, the `AuthUser` object will look like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const user = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // User data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id: "cluqs9qyh00007cn73apj4hp7",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  address: "Some address",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Auth methods specific data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  identities: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    email: null,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    google: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      id: "1117XXXX1301972049448",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**User Signed Up with Email**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the user has only the email identity, the `AuthUser` object will look like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const user = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // User data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id: "cluqsex9500017cn7i2hwsg17",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  address: "Some address",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Auth methods specific data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  identities: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    email: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      id: "user@app.com",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      isEmailVerified: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      emailVerificationSentAt: "2024-04-08T10:06:02.204Z",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      passwordResetSentAt: null,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    google: null,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In the examples above, you can see the `identities` object contains the `email` and `google` objects. The `email` object contains the email-related data and the `google` object contains the Google-related data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info[Make sure to check if the data exists]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Before accessing some auth method's data, you'll need to check if that data exists for the user and then access it:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (user.identities.google !== null) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const userId = user.identities.google.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You need to do this because if a user didn't sign up with some auth method, the data for that auth method will be `null`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's look at the data for each of the available auth methods:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Username & password](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const usernameIdentity = user.identities.username\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Username that the user used to sign up, e.g. "fluffyllama"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  usernameIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Email](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const emailIdentity = user.identities.email\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Email address the user used to sign up, e.g. "fluffyllama@app.com".\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  emailIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // `true` if the user has verified their email address.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  emailIdentity.isEmailVerified\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Datetime when the email verification email was sent.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  emailIdentity.emailVerificationSentAt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Datetime when the last password reset email was sent.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  emailIdentity.passwordResetSentAt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Google](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/google) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const googleIdentity = user.identities.google\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Google User ID for example "123456789012345678901"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  googleIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [GitHub](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/github) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const githubIdentity = user.identities.github\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // GitHub User ID for example "12345678"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  githubIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Keycloak](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/keycloak) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const keycloakIdentity = user.identities.keycloak\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Keycloak User ID for example "12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  keycloakIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Discord](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/discord) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const discordIdentity = user.identities.discord\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Discord User ID for example "80351110224678912"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  discordIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you support multiple auth methods, you'll need to find which identity exists for the user and then access its data:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (user.identities.email !== null) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const email = user.identities.email.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} else if (user.identities.google !== null) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const googleId = user.identities.google.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### `getFirstProviderUserId` Helper\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `getFirstProviderUserId` method returns the first user ID that it finds for the user. For example if the user has signed up with email, it will return the email. If the user has signed up with Google, it will return the Google ID.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This can be useful if you support multiple authentication methods and you need *any* ID that identifies the user in your app.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/MainPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { type AuthUser } from "wasp/auth"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const MainPage = ({ user }: { user: AuthUser }) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const userId = user.getFirstProviderUserId()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/tasks.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const createTask: CreateTask<...>  = async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const userId = context.user.getFirstProviderUserId()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\\* Multiple identities per user will be possible in the future and then the `getFirstProviderUserId` method will return the ID of the first identity that it finds without any guarantees about which one it will be.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Including the User with Other Entities\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Sometimes, you might want to include the user's data when fetching other entities. For example, you might want to include the user's data with the tasks they have created.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We'll mention the `auth` and the `identities` relations which we will explain in more detail later in the [Entities Explained](#entities-explained) section.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::caution[Be careful about sensitive data]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You'll need to include the `auth` and the `identities` relations to get the full auth data about the user. However, you should keep in mind that the `providerData` field in the `identities` can contain sensitive data like the user's hashed password (in case of email or username auth), so you will likely want to exclude it if you are returning those values to the client.\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You can include the full user's data with other entities using the `include` option in the Prisma queries:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/tasks.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const getAllTasks = (async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return context.entities.Task.findMany({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    orderBy: { id: "desc" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    select: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      id: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      title: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      user: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        include: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          auth: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            include: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              identities: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                // Including only the `providerName` and `providerUserId` fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                select: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                  providerName: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                  providerUserId: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}) satisfies tasks.GetAllQuery<{}, {}>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you have some **piece of the auth data that you want to access frequently** (for example the `username`), it's best to store it at the top level of the `User` entity.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For example, save the `username` or `email` as a property on the `User` and you'll be able to access it without including the `auth` and `identities` fields. We show an example in the [Defining Extra Fields on the User Entity](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#1-defining-extra-fields) section of the docs.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Getting Auth Data from the User Object\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you have the `user` object with the `auth` and `identities` fields, it can be a bit tedious to obtain the auth data (like username or Google ID) from it:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/MainPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function MainPage() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <div className="tasks">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      {tasks.map((task) => (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <div key={task.id} className="task">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          {task.title} by {task.user.auth?.identities[0].providerUserId}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      ))}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp offers a few helper methods to access the user's auth data when you retrieve the `user` like this. They are `getUsername`, `getEmail` and `getFirstProviderUserId`. They can be used both on the client and the server.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### `getUsername`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It accepts the `user` object and if the user signed up with the [Username & password](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass) auth method, it returns the username or `null` otherwise. The `user` object needs to have the `auth` and the `identities` relations included.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/MainPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getUsername } from "wasp/auth"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function MainPage() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <div className="tasks">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      {tasks.map((task) => (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <div key={task.id} className="task">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          {task.title} by {getUsername(task.user)}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      ))}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### `getEmail`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It accepts the `user` object and if the user signed up with the [Email](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email) auth method, it returns the email or `null` otherwise. The `user` object needs to have the `auth` and the `identities` relations included.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/MainPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getEmail } from "wasp/auth"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function MainPage() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <div className="tasks">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      {tasks.map((task) => (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <div key={task.id} className="task">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          {task.title} by {getEmail(task.user)}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      ))}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``'[39m... 10257 more characters
                  }
                ]
              },
              providerOptions: {
                vertex: {
                  thoughtSignature: [32m''[39m
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        },

        {

          content: [
            {
              type: [32m'tool-result'[39m,
              toolCallId: [32m'7rGc2Dl87bFmT4AH'[39m,
              toolName: [32m'webFetch'[39m,
              output: {
                type: [32m'content'[39m,
                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'Title: \n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'URL Source: https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/data-model/databases.md\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Markdown Content:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://wasp.sh/llms.txt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'---\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Databases\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"[Entities](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/data-model/entities), [Operations](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/data-model/operations/overview) and [Automatic CRUD](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/data-model/crud) together make a high-level interface for working with your app's data. Still, all that data has to live somewhere, so let's see how Wasp deals with databases.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Supported Database Backends\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp supports multiple database backends. We'll list and explain each one.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### SQLite\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The default database Wasp uses is [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you create a new Wasp project, the `schema.prisma` file will have SQLite as the default database provider:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```prisma title="schema.prisma"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'datasource db {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  provider = "sqlite"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Read more about how Wasp uses the Prisma schema file in the [Prisma schema file](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/data-model/prisma-file) section.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you use the SQLite database, Wasp sets the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable for you.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"SQLite is a great way to get started with a new project because it doesn't require any configuration, but Wasp can only use it in development. Once you want to deploy your Wasp app to production, you'll need to switch to PostgreSQL and stick with it.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Fortunately, migrating from SQLite to PostgreSQL is pretty simple, and we have [a guide](#migrating-from-sqlite-to-postgresql) to help you.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### PostgreSQL\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"[PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) is the most advanced open-source database and one of the most popular databases overall. It's been in active development for 20+ years. Therefore, if you're looking for a battle-tested database, look no further.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To use PostgreSQL with Wasp, set the provider to `"postgresql"` in the `schema.prisma` file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```prisma title="schema.prisma"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'datasource db {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  provider = "postgresql"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Read more about how Wasp uses the Prisma schema file in the [Prisma schema file](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/data-model/prisma-file) section.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You'll have to ensure a database instance is running during development to use PostgreSQL. Wasp needs access to your database for commands such as `wasp start` or `wasp db migrate-dev`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We cover all supported ways of connecting to a database in [the next section](#connecting-to-a-database).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Connecting to a Database\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### SQLite\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you are using SQLite, you don't need to do anything special to connect to the database. Wasp will take care of it for you.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### PostgreSQL\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you are using PostgreSQL, Wasp supports two ways of connecting to a database:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. For managed experience, let Wasp spin up a ready-to-go development database for you.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. For more control, you can specify a database URL and connect to an existing database that you provisioned yourself.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Using the Dev Database provided by Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The command `wasp start db` will start a default PostgreSQL dev database for you.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Your Wasp app will automatically connect to it, just keep `wasp start db` running in the background. Also, make sure that:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- You have [Docker installed](https://www.docker.com/get-started/) and it's available in your `PATH`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"- The port `5432` isn't taken.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::tip\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In case you might want to connect to the dev database through the external tool like `psql` or [pgAdmin](https://www.pgadmin.org/), the credentials are printed in the console when you run `wasp db start`, at the very beginning.\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'##### Customising the dev database {#custom-database}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The Wasp development database uses the [PostgreSQL 18 Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/_/postgres/tags?name=18) by default, and will set up its data volumes according to their guidance.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to customise the development database, you can use the following options:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `--db-image`: Specify a custom Docker image\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  Useful for PostgreSQL extensions or specific versions (for example, PostGIS, pgvector, etc.).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `--db-volume-mount-path`: Specify the volume mount path inside the container\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  You only need to set this option if your custom `--db-image` is based on **PostgreSQL 17 or older** (check the `postgres:15` example below).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"  If the volume mount path is incorrect, the data won't be persisted in your development database.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Here are some examples of customising the development database:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```bash\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Use default PostgreSQL image:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp start db\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Same as:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp start db --db-image postgres:18\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Use PostgreSQL with PostGIS extension for geographic data:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp start db --db-image postgis/postgis:18-3.6 \n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Use PostgreSQL with pgvector extension for AI embeddings:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp start db --db-image pgvector/pgvector:pg18\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Use PostgreSQL version 15 (requires different volume path):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp start db --db-image postgres:15 --db-volume-mount-path /var/lib/postgresql/data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::note\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The custom Docker image you specify must use the `POSTGRES_DB`, `POSTGRES_USER`, and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` environment variables when configuring the database. Wasp will use those values when connecting to the database. We recommend basing your image on the official [PostgreSQL Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/_/postgres), as it automatically uses these environment variables to set up the database name, user, and password.\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Connecting to an existing database\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you want to spin up your own dev database (or connect to an external one), you can tell Wasp about it using the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable. Wasp will use the value of `DATABASE_URL` as a connection string.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The easiest way to set the necessary `DATABASE_URL` environment variable is by adding it to the [.env.server](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/project/env-vars) file in the root dir of your Wasp project (if that file doesn't yet exist, create it):\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```env title=".env.server"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/mydb\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Alternatively, you can set it inline when running `wasp` (this applies to all environment variables):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```bash\n'[39m +
                      [32m'DATABASE_URL=<my-db-url> wasp ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This trick is useful for running a certain `wasp` command on a specific database. For example, you could do:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```bash\n'[39m +
                      [32m'DATABASE_URL=<production-db-url> wasp db seed myProductionSeed\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This command seeds the data for a fresh staging or production database. Read more about [seeding the database](#seeding-the-database).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Migrating from SQLite to PostgreSQL\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To run your Wasp app in production, you'll need to switch from SQLite to PostgreSQL.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Set the provider to `"postgresql"` in the `schema.prisma` file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'   ```prisma title="schema.prisma"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'   datasource db {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'     provider = "postgresql"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'     url      = env("DATABASE_URL")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'   }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'   // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'   ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. Delete all the old migrations, since they are SQLite migrations and can't be used with PostgreSQL, as well as the SQLite database by running [`wasp clean`](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/general/cli#project-commands):\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'   ```bash\n'[39m +
                      [32m'   rm -r migrations/\n'[39m +
                      [32m'   wasp clean\n'[39m +
                      [32m'   ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Ensure your new database is running (check the [section on connecting to a database](#connecting-to-a-database) to see how). Leave it running, since we need it for the next step.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. In a different terminal, run `wasp db migrate-dev` to apply the changes and create a new initial migration.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'5. That is it, you are all done!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Seeding the Database\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Database seeding** is a term used for populating the database with some initial data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Seeding is most commonly used for:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Getting the development database into a state convenient for working and testing.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Initializing any database (`dev`, `staging`, or `prod`) with essential data it requires to operate. For example, populating the Currency table with default currencies, or the Country table with all available countries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Writing a Seed Function\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can define as many **seed functions** as you want in an array under the `db.seeds` field:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { devSeedSimple, prodSeed } from "./src/dbSeeds" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  name: "MyApp",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  db: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    seeds: [devSeedSimple, prodSeed],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Each seed function must be an async function that takes one argument, `prisma`, which is a [Prisma Client](https://www.prisma.io/docs/concepts/components/prisma-client/crud) instance used to interact with the database. This is the same Prisma Client instance that Wasp uses internally.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since a seed function falls under server-side code, it can import other server-side functions. This is convenient because you might want to seed the database using Actions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's an example of a seed function that imports an Action:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { createTask } from "./actions.js"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { DbSeedFn } from "wasp/server"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { sanitizeAndSerializeProviderData } from "wasp/server/auth"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { AuthUser } from "wasp/auth"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { PrismaClient } from "wasp/server"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const devSeedSimple: DbSeedFn = async (prisma) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const user = await createUser(prisma, {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    username: "RiuTheDog",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    password: "bark1234",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  await createTask(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    { description: "Chase the cat", isDone: false },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    { user, entities: { Task: prisma.task } }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async function createUser(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  prisma: PrismaClient,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  data: { username: string, password: string }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'): Promise<AuthUser> {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const newUser = await prisma.user.create({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    data: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      auth: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        create: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          identities: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            create: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              providerName: "username",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              providerUserId: data.username,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              providerData: await sanitizeAndSerializeProviderData<"username">({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                hashedPassword: data.password\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              }),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return newUser\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp exports a type called `DbSeedFn` which you can use to easily type your seeding function. Wasp defines `DbSeedFn` like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```typesc'[39m... 3191 more characters
                  }
                ]

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'---\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We'll explain what Queries are and how to use them. If you're looking for a detailed API specification, skip ahead to the [API Reference](#api-reference).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You can use Queries to fetch data from the server. They shouldn't modify the server's state. Fetching all comments on a blog post, a list of users that liked a video, information about a single product based on its ID... All of these are perfect use cases for a Query.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::tip\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Queries are fairly similar to Actions in terms of their API. Therefore, if you're already familiar with Actions, you might find reading the entire guide repetitive.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We instead recommend skipping ahead and only reading [the differences between Queries and Actions](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/data-model/operations/actions#differences-between-queries-and-actions), and consulting the [API Reference](#api-reference) as needed.\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Working with Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You declare queries in the Wasp file and implement them using NodeJS. Wasp not only runs these queries within the server's context but also creates code that enables you to call them from any part of your codebase, whether it's on the client or server side.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This means you don't have to build an HTTP API for your query, manage server-side request handling, or even deal with client-side response handling and caching. Instead, just concentrate on implementing the business logic inside your query, and let Wasp handle the rest!\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a Query, you must:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Declare the Query in Wasp using the `query` spec.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. Define the Query's NodeJS implementation.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"After completing these two steps, you'll be able to use the Query from any point in your code.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Specifying Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a Query in Wasp, we begin with a `query` spec.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's declare two Queries - one to fetch all tasks, and another to fetch tasks based on a filter, such as whether a task is done:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, query } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getAllTasks, getFilteredTasks } from "./src/queries" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    query(getAllTasks),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    query(getFilteredTasks),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you want to know about all supported options for the `query` spec, take a look at the [API Reference](#api-reference).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::note\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When `main.wasp.ts` needs to point to your code, it uses imports like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Notice the `with { type: "ref" }` part at the end of the import statement. This tells Wasp to treat the import as a reference to your app\'s code, without running the imported code. For more details and examples, see [reference imports](https://wasp.sh/docs/general/spec#reference-imports).\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You might have noticed that we told Wasp to import Query implementations that don't yet exist. Don't worry about that for now. We'll write the implementations imported from `queries.ts` in the next section.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's a good idea to start with the high-level concept (the Query spec in the Wasp file) and only then deal with the implementation details (the Query's implementation in JavaScript).\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"After declaring a Wasp Query, Wasp derives the Query's name from the function you pass to `query`. For example, `query(getFilteredTasks)` creates a Query named `getFilteredTasks`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Two important things then happen:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Wasp **generates a server-side NodeJS function** with the Query's name.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Wasp **generates a client-side JavaScript function** with the Query's name (e.g., `getFilteredTasks`). This function takes a single optional argument - an object containing any serializable data you wish to use inside the Query. Wasp will send this object over the network and pass it into the Query's implementation as its first positional argument (more on this when we look at the implementations). Such an abstraction works thanks to an HTTP API route handler Wasp generates on the server, which calls the Query's NodeJS implementation under the hood.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Generating these two functions ensures a similar calling interface across the entire app (both client and server).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Implementing Queries in Node\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Now that we've declared the Query, what remains is to implement it. We've instructed Wasp to look for the Queries' implementations in the file `src/queries.ts`, so that's where we should export them from.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's how you might implement the previously declared Queries `getAllTasks` and `getFilteredTasks`:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/queries.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { type GetAllTasks, type GetFilteredTasks } from "wasp/server/operations"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Task = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id: number\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  description: string\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  isDone: boolean\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// our "database"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const tasks: Task[] = [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  { id: 1, description: "Buy some eggs", isDone: true },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  { id: 2, description: "Make an omelette", isDone: false },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  { id: 3, description: "Eat breakfast", isDone: false },\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"// You don't need to use the arguments if you don't need them\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export const getAllTasks: GetAllTasks<void, Task[]> = () => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return tasks\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"// The 'args' object is something sent by the caller (most often from the client)\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export const getFilteredTasks: GetFilteredTasks<\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  Pick<Task, "isDone">,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  Task[]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> = (args) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const { isDone } = args\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return tasks.filter((task) => task.isDone === isDone)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info[Payload constraints]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp uses [superjson](https://github.com/flightcontrolhq/superjson) under the hood. This means you're not limited to only sending and receiving JSON payloads.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp will automatically handle the serialization and deserialization [for all the data types that superjson supports](https://github.com/flightcontrolhq/superjson#decimaljs--prismadecimal:~\\:text=Superjson%20supports%20many%20extra%20types) (like `biging`, `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, etc.), and for [Prisma.Decimal](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/special-fields-and-types#working-with-decimal).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"As long as you're annotating your Operations with the correct automatically generated types, TypeScript ensures your payloads are valid (i.e., Wasp knows how to serialize and deserialize them).\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Type support for Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp automatically generates the types `GetAllTasks` and `GetFilteredTasks` based on your Wasp file's specs:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `GetAllTasks` is a generic type automatically generated by Wasp, based on the Query spec for `getAllTasks`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `GetFilteredTasks` is also a generic type automatically generated by Wasp, based on the Query spec for `getFilteredTasks`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Use these types to type the Query's implementation. It's optional but very helpful since doing so properly types the Query's context.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, TypeScript will know the `context.entities` object must include the `Task` entity. TypeScript also knows whether the `context` object includes user information (it depends on whether your Query uses auth).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The generated types are generic and accept two optional type arguments: `Input` and `Output`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. `Input` - The argument (the payload) received by the Query function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. `Output` - The Query function's return type.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Use these type arguments to type the Query's inputs and outputs.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Explanation for the example above\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The above code says that the Query `getAllTasks` doesn't expect any arguments (its input type is `void`), but it does return a list of tasks (its output type is `Task[]`).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'On the other hand, the Query `getFilteredTasks` expects an object of type `{ isDone: boolean }`. This type is derived from the `Task` entity type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you don't care about typing the Query's inputs and outputs, you can omit both type arguments. TypeScript will then infer the most general types (`never` for the input and `unknown` for the output).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Specifying `Input` or `Output` is completely optional, but we highly recommended it. Doing so gives you:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Type support for the arguments and the return value inside the implementation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- **Full-stack type safety**. We'll explore what this means when we discuss calling the Query from the client.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Read more about type support for implementing Queries in the [API Reference](#implementing-queries).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::tip[Inferring the return type]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If don't want to explicitly type the Query's return value, the `satisfies` keyword tells TypeScript to infer it automatically:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```typescript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const getFoo = (async (_args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const foos = await context.entities.Foo.findMany()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    foos,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    message: "Here are some foos!",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    queriedAt: new Date(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}) satisfies GetFoo\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'From the snippet above, TypeScript knows:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. The correct type for `context`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. The Query's return type is `{ foos: Foo[], message: string, queriedAt: Date }`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you don't need the context, you can skip specifying the Query's type (and arguments):\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```typescript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const getFoo = () => ({ name: "Foo", date: new Date() })\n'[39m +
